extraction.methodology_summary: The paper constructs a quality-adjusted real estate price index for Japanese municipalities from 2005 onwards using hedonic regression on over 5 million transactions. It extracts alternative socio-economic and demographic factors (such as net migration, taxable income growth, and new dwelling ratios) from the SSDS and MLIT datasets. Simple long-short portfolios and Transformer time series models are then tested using these variables to predict future municipal real estate returns.
extraction.universe: 1100 municipalities across Japan (restricted to top 500 most populous in long-short factor experiments)

key_findings: Alternative data variables such as net migration ratio, taxable income growth, and new dwelling ratios can successfully forecast real estate performance across Japanese municipalities.
Long-short investment strategies based on these fundamental alternative data factors generated positive returns with low volatility.

Time series Transformer models effectively harness non-linear temporal and spatial relationships in alternative datasets, achieving an R-squared of 0.28 when predicting risk-adjusted returns four years ahead.
